A legal treatise is a scholarly legal publication containing all the law relating to a particular area, such as criminal law or trusts and estates . There is no fixed usage on what books qualify as a "legal treatise", with the term being used broadly to define books written for practicing attorneys and judges , textbooks for law students, and explanatory texts for laypersons. [ 1 ] The treatise may generally be loose leaf bound with rings or posts so that updates to laws covered by the treatise and annotated by the editor may be added by the subscriber to the legal treatise.
